title: The Hall: playback and programme
promise: Playing a recording, choosing from the programme, and the player bar that stays on every page.

steps.title: Play
steps.text: Play starts Satie’s First Gymnopédie; the next recording follows automatically. Space pauses; N and P change pieces when no control has focus.

steps.title: Score view
steps.text: Choose Score. The gold highlight marks the bar being played; selecting a bar plays from there.

steps.title: Programme
steps.text: Open the programme to choose an evening or a single recording. The full concert follows the composers’ birth order and keeps the movements of a work together.

steps.title: Close the programme
steps.text: Closing the programme does not stop playback. The question-mark button reopens this tour.

steps.title: Player bar
steps.text: The player bar stays on every page of the site; playback continues while a chapter or lesson is open.

title: Score view: Satie’s First Gymnopédie
promise: The engraved score with the current bar highlighted, and the same music in the Notes view.

steps.title: Play
steps.text: Play starts the First Gymnopédie.

steps.title: Score
steps.text: Choose Score. The gold highlight moves through the printed bars with the recording.

steps.title: Score source
steps.text: The caption names the score; its timing is aligned automatically and has not yet been checked by ear. The § opens the edition and licence. Selecting a bar plays from there.

steps.title: Notes
steps.text: Choose Notes to show each voice in its own colour, with pitches and lengths taken from the score.

title: Views of Beethoven’s Fifth
promise: The Score, Notes, Orchestra, Form and Sound views, on the first movement of Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony.

steps.title: Play
steps.text: Play starts the first movement of Beethoven’s Fifth; the view can be changed while the recording continues.

steps.title: Score
steps.text: Choose Score for the engraved score; the gold highlight marks the bar being played.

steps.title: Notes
steps.text: Choose Notes for the score’s pitches and note lengths as coloured lines, one colour per voice.

steps.title: Orchestra
steps.text: Choose Orchestra. Each instrument group lights up while its part sounds. The same view is available for Boléro.

steps.title: Form
steps.text: Choose Form for the sections, with arcs joining each theme to its return. Selecting a section plays from its start.

steps.title: Sound
steps.text: Choose Sound for the recording’s frequencies and loudness, with an estimate of its harmony.

steps.title: Enlarge the view
steps.text: F, or Enlarge under the view, fills the hall with it; F again restores it.

steps.title: Player bar
steps.text: Playback continues while a chapter or lesson is open; the player bar has a pause button on every page.

title: Joins between sections
promise: The silence before the horn call in Beethoven’s Fifth, and how the score prepares it.

steps.title: Joins
steps.text: Choose Joins. The tab describes how each section leads into the next: a silence, a new chord, a change of instrument.

steps.title: Play the first join
steps.text: This button plays the passage leading into the silence before the horn call.

steps.title: Timeline markers
steps.text: Each diamond on the timeline marks a join; selecting one plays the passage around it.

steps.title: Listening notes
steps.text: Choose Listening notes. The notes follow the recording, with a card at each join.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.text: Open Evidence for the source of the note: the score, the recording or a historical account.

title: Recording details and sources
promise: The session, the original disc, the digital transfer and a citation for one recording.

steps.title: Recording
steps.text: Choose Recording for the performers, session, original disc and digital transfer.

steps.title: Evidence labels
steps.text: Documented facts have a cited source; inferred ones are reasoned from evidence. Disputed entries give alternatives, and unknown entries are marked Unknown.

steps.title: Other performances
steps.text: Each link opens a comparison of the same music; each card there identifies its performance and transfer.

steps.title: Citation
steps.text: A citation with the performer, the recording source and the Hall link.

steps.title: Download the register
steps.text: The recording register as CSV or JSON, with separate fields for facts, evidence labels, sources and alternatives.

title: Comparing two recordings
promise: Rachmaninoff’s 1919 and 1928 recordings of his Prelude in C♯ minor, switched mid-phrase.

steps.title: The 1919 recording
steps.text: Select the Edison recording; its clock is the reference for this comparison.

steps.title: Play
steps.text: Play starts the selected recording. Selecting another card continues from the matching point in that recording.

steps.title: Move to 0:42
steps.text: Move to 42 seconds in the reference recording, after the opening lead-in.

steps.title: Switch to 1928
steps.text: Select the 1928 electrical Victor recording; the phrase continues from the same point.

steps.title: Tempo map
steps.text: Above 1×, the performer takes longer over the same music than the reference; below it, less time.

steps.title: Passages
steps.text: Each passage plays in every available recording, one after another.

title: The Dies irae in the Web of Influence
promise: The chant and its use in Rachmaninoff’s Isle of the Dead.

steps.title: Dies irae
steps.text: Choose Dies irae to highlight the works that use the chant; each gold line opens a connection and its sources.

steps.title: The chant
steps.text: Play the opening of the chant in synthesised sound; the caption explains the rhythm and tempo chosen.

steps.title: Isle of the Dead
steps.text: Open the Isle of the Dead connection for where the chant appears in Rachmaninoff’s music.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.text: The evidence note gives the basis for the connection between the chant and the Isle of the Dead.

steps.title: Sources and link
steps.text: Each source opens in a new tab; the page address links directly to this connection.

title: Vivaldi’s RV 522 and Bach’s BWV 593
promise: The opening of Vivaldi’s concerto and of Bach’s organ transcription, as playable score examples.

steps.title: The two works
steps.text: Bach transcribed Vivaldi’s Concerto RV 522 for organ as BWV 593.

steps.title: Vivaldi: first violin
steps.text: Play the first violin’s opening two bars in A minor, in synthesised sound.

steps.title: Bach: organ
steps.text: Play Bach’s uppermost line; the caption names the omitted voices and links to the full score.

steps.title: Sources
steps.text: The sources link to the full scores of both works.

title: The Map: Vienna in 1900 and Mahler
promise: Vienna in 1900, and Mahler’s places in date order.

steps.title: Year
steps.text: The Map opens at 1900; the slider changes the year.

steps.title: Composer
steps.text: Mahler is selected; the numbered list gives dates and sources for each place on his map.

steps.title: Recordings
steps.text: Play a work linked to this place, or choose another recording by the composer.

steps.title: Encounters
steps.text: Open Encounters for the composers whose dates overlap in the selected city.

steps.title: City records
steps.text: The card gives dates and sources. The City menu selects another place.

title: Guided journey: Vienna, 1900
promise: Recordings, paintings and sources for Vienna around 1900, station by station.

steps.title: Begin
steps.text: Begin plays the stations in order; Pause stops at the current station for reading or looking at a painting.

steps.title: Station text
steps.text: Each station pairs a recording excerpt with a text and an exhibit; short notes appear as the excerpt plays.

steps.title: Sources
steps.text: Open Sources & recording for the excerpt’s times, its sources and a link to the full recording in the Hall.

steps.title: Next station
steps.text: Next or a numbered station changes station; after the tour the arrow keys do the same. The current station is saved in this browser.

title: Composer chapter: Mahler
promise: Contents, influences, further reading and citation in Mahler’s chapter.

steps.title: Contents
steps.text: The contents link to Mahler’s life, music, works, places and sources.

steps.title: Influences
steps.text: Each connection opens its account and sources in the Web of Influence.

steps.title: Further reading
steps.text: Each book, catalogue and article has a short note.

steps.title: Cite this page
steps.text: Open a Chicago reference or BibTeX entry for this page.

steps.title: Copy the citation
steps.text: Copy the Chicago citation and set the access date to the day the page was read.

title: Glossary and search
promise: The sonata form entry with its recorded example, definitions in the text, and site search.

steps.title: Sonata form
steps.text: The entry defines sonata form with Beethoven’s Fifth as the example, and links to related terms and passages.

steps.title: Example
steps.text: Play starts the passage described in the note.

steps.title: Definitions in the text
steps.text: Hover over an underlined term, reach it with Tab or tap it to open a definition; its link leads to the glossary entry.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Search, or the / key, finds composers, works, recordings, terms and guide tours. On a small screen, Search is inside Menu.

title: Return Lab: exposition and recapitulation
promise: The exposition and recapitulation of the first movement of Beethoven’s Fifth, bar by bar.
feature: Return Lab · paired passages · bar charts

steps.title: Passage A
steps.text: Choose A for the marked passage from the exposition.

steps.title: Passage B
steps.text: Choose B for the corresponding passage in the recapitulation, where Beethoven brings the music towards the home key.

steps.title: Bar grid
steps.text: Matching bars share a column; colours separate the voices, and hatched gaps mark bars with no counterpart.

steps.title: Score and performance
steps.text: Beethoven’s written changes beside the time each bar takes in this performance.
